papers.title: CFTs with Large Virasoro Primary Gaps
papers.abstract: We construct the first explicit examples of compact unitary bosonic full conformal field theories (CFTs) in two dimensions with a unique vacuum and an all-spin Virasoro-primary gap greater than two. Our constructions use asymmetric orbifolds of lattice CFTs built from even unimodular lattices of sufficiently large minimum norm, ensuring that no charged state lies below the desired gap. papers.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
papers.abstract: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. papers.title: Complete Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-handed Neutrino Loops
papers.abstract: We study the complete cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement. These CC signals are induced by the inflaton-right-handed-neutrino interaction and can be extracted in the collinear squeezed configuration, which allows the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop to be factorized into the hard and soft parts. papers.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Applications such as visual accessibility agents and robotics require answering questions about recent video content promptly, over a bounded window of past frames (e.g., the last two minutes). Hybrid vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave attention with linear recurrent layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), are attractive for this setting, but maintaining a sliding window is expensive. papers.title: Expressivity of two-dimensional Gaussian fermion tensor network states
papers.abstract: Tensor network states (TNS) provide a family of efficiently compressed approximations to physically relevant many-body quantum states. An important quantity that characterizes the computational resources required by a TNS is its bond dimension. While in one dimension an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy guarantees an exact matrix product state representation with a bond dimension independent of the system size, an analogous statement does not hold for general states in two dimensions (2D).
